name: prompt-response-optimizer
context: Systems that iteratively refine prompts or response templates based on observed outputs, success rates, or user feedback. Rather than treating prompts as fixed, the system treats them as tunable parameters — adjusting prompt construction, instruction ordering, or response schemas to maximize measured quality over multiple rounds.
benefits: Improves output quality without changing model architecture
Adapts prompts to the specific distribution of inputs
Can discover prompt strategies that human engineers miss
Enables automated A/B testing of prompt variations
tradeoffs: Requires a feedback signal (human labels, task success, evaluator scores)
Prompt optimization can be sample-inefficient — many attempts before improvement
Overfitting to the evaluation metric can degrade real-world performance
Optimized prompts may not generalize to out-of-distribution inputs
use_cases: Tool definition refinement: a prompt is tuned based on observed tool call success rates
RAG query optimization: prompt templates are refined based on retrieval precision metrics
Response format tuning: JSON schema instructions are adjusted based on parsing success rates
System prompt optimization: agent instructions are refined based on task completion rates
avoid_when: No feedback signal is available to evaluate prompt quality
Inputs are so diverse that a single optimized prompt cannot cover the distribution
Latency constraints require keeping prompts static between runs
anti_patterns: Optimizing for a metric that does not correlate with real task quality
Keeping prompts static when the input distribution has changed significantly
No evaluation harness — changes are deployed without measuring impact
design_principles: Prompt changes must be tracked in version control alongside code
The optimization target must correlate with real-world task quality
Deployments should use shadow mode to test prompts before full rollout
best_practices: Start with a simple heuristic (word ordering, few-shot examples) before automated optimization
Use a held-out eval set to detect overfitting to the optimization signal
Maintain a prompt changelog so regressions can be traced to specific changes
references: Khattab et al., DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines, 2023 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03714
